minutes.headline: Board ratified a police sergeant and assistant town accountant, extended health opt-out pilot, deferred building fee vote
minutes.summary: The board heard two complaints in public comment, ratified two appointments, and heard the Building Commissioner's proposed new fee schedules for building, electrical, plumbing and gas permits, with the vote deferred two weeks for public input. It voted to extend the health insurance opt-out pilot through fiscal year 25 and signed the unused levy capacity form. It then went into executive session to review old minutes and adjourn.

Read a statement complaining about the cemetery commission chair's conduct at a November 30th meeting and a reported fuel spill.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted 5-0 to extend the health insurance opt-out pilot program through fiscal year 25.
The board deferred its vote on the Building Commissioner's new fee schedules for building, electrical, plumbing and gas permits, to allow two weeks of public review.
The proposed schedules raise the commercial rate and minimums, move sheet metal permits to a per-thousand rate, and raise the plumbing and gas fees set in 1987.
The board ratified, 5-0 by roll call, a police sergeant promotion and the appointment of an assistant town accountant.
The board heard two public comments with complaints about the police chief and the cemetery commission chair.

why_it_matters: Anyone pulling a building, electrical, plumbing or gas permit, or applying for a stop work or occupancy permit, could pay different fees if the schedule is adopted, and the vote has not yet happened.
The opt-out pilot extension keeps in place the arrangement that the board tied to the public employee committee agreement, which bears on what the town spends on employee health insurance.
watch_next: The vote on the building department fee schedule, expected at the December 19th Select Board meeting, with the schedule to be posted on the town website beforehand.
The Building Commissioner's report back, about a year later, on how the new fees are working.
